Someone once asked me why I chose Qin Changge, and why I ultimately chose Nirvana in Flames.

What first drew me in wasn't where the story would lead, nor who Changge would eventually become. It was a much simpler question: What does a person have to go through to become the person she is today?

During the long preparation period, I had no idea how to get close to her. Once filming began, the distance between us felt even greater than I had imagined. For much of that time, I felt I still hadn't truly become her...

Until one day, as I delivered a particular line, I suddenly connected with the state of mind she had at the very beginning of the story. From that moment on, I felt I had finally begun to understand the path her fate was destined to take, and why it had to unfold that way.

What Changge left me with wasn't a definitive answer, but a quiet kind of strength. She is rarely in a hurry to prove herself or explain her intentions. Like a silent traveler, she simply keeps moving forward.

These past few months with her have meant so much to me. As I gradually drew closer to her, she was quietly changing me, too.

Thank you, Nirvana in Flames, and thank you to everyone who helped bring this story to life — the director, the screenwriters, all my fellow cast members, and every single person working behind the scenes. My thanks also go to the platform and production company for giving us this opportunity to meet. It was through everyone's dedication and collective efforts that Qin Changge truly came to life.

If she could really hear me, there's something I would want to tell her:

Because of this story, there will be more and more people in this world who understand you.

I hope you know that.

Thank you for entrusting me with all your silence, restraint, judgment, and moments of defiance over these past months — for showing me that growth isn't built on empty words or slogans, but shaped by one choice after another.

You are not strong because pain shaped you.
You made it here through clarity, through knowing where to draw the line, and through refusing to back down, time and time again.

Thank you for showing me that breaking free from control is not the same as winning; the true way forward is to reclaim the power to define yourself.

This chapter of the journey has come to an end.
May you never again feel the need to prove anything,
nor ever have to rely on pain to remember who you are.

My heartfelt thanks to everyone who gave Zhou Yan the space to breathe throughout this journey —

Thank you to Youku and Dunqi Studio for their wholehearted support of this production, allowing such a complex and powerful character to be treated with the care and seriousness she deserves, portrayed with depth and nuance, and given the space for her story to unfold.

Thank you to director Gao Bingquan for his precise understanding of the character, capturing her restraint, her pauses, and the subtlest shifts in her emotional state through the lens.

Thank you to action director Chen Jiafu for his exacting standards and meticulous attention to every movement, ensuring that each action served the character and created a distinctive presence and energy unique to Origin.

Thank you to the art department for creating such immersive spaces, transforming the "Gate of Rebirth" from an abstract concept into a tangible reality.

And thank you to all my fellow cast members —

From the emotional bonds shared with the "younger brothers and sisters," to the sense of order and boundaries established by the "police team," and the dramatic tension brought by the "gang of thieves," each of you helped build a complete and believable foundation for Zhou Yan's world, somewhere between fantasy and reality.

On this journey, Zhou Yan has finally found her way out.

At this very moment, may Be Reborn: Origin break through every barrier, face the abyss, and find new life beyond it.

Happy wrap, Zhou Yan. I look forward to meeting you again before long.

The story of Kill Me Love Me is drawing to a close, and it's time to say goodbye to Meilin.
Meilin is fierce and headstrong. That is why, ten years ago, the little "beggar" from Qingzhou went after the Butcher General, the very person she believed to be her enemy, without a moment's hesitation.
She is intelligent and clear-minded. As an assassin trained to die, she fears death, yet knows she must stay alive. She can also choose to shoulder the hope of peace between two nations, urging Jinghe to leave the past behind and move forward.
She is kind and sensitive. She takes in every bit of kindness shown to her by those around her, and has the strength to give even more in return.
She is free-spirited. When it comes to love, she is sincere and wholehearted, stubbornly guarding that little glimmer of light behind her. Yet, after all the twists and turns of love and hatred, she is also able to let go, take on a new name, and choose to live for herself.
People say she is like a flower that refuses to die, blooming amid the ruins, and like fireworks bursting brilliantly in the darkness.
Some time ago, a journalist asked me: If Meilin were given another chance at life, or lived in a parallel universe, would she try to make up for the regrets of this lifetime?
I don't think Meilin would have any regrets.
She had hated fiercely, loved wholeheartedly, and given everything she had. She had lived freely, always staying true to her heart. She only gets one life, and she lived it to the fullest, without holding anything back!
The snow falls softly over Qingzhou. Meilin's deepest wish in this lifetime has finally come true. She asks for nothing more.
Goodbye, Meilin.

One day at about ten in the morning, in a corner of the Court of State Ceremonial, Meilin wandered aimlessly down a corridor, not knowing where she was going. She turned her head and saw flowers, grass and a lake; sunlight fell right on her face. She slowed her steps and looked at everything, and for the first time felt a moment that belonged to her alone. She didn't want to lose herself in it, nor did she try to hold on to it; she just kept looking. She didn't know what she loved — that love was buried very, very deep in her heart, and it took the story of 《Kill Me Love Me》 for it to slowly surface, from blurry to clearer and clearer…
"Chun" (spring) is the middle character of her mother's name, Liu Chunxi. It is the "sprouting" and "life" of the story.
"Hua" (flower) is the love in her heart. It is the "hope" of the story.
"Yan" is everything the story holds.

Second, this script was my choice; it wasn't a filler show squeezed in because the schedule between 《Something Just Like This》 and 《Legacy》 was tight. It was the uniqueness of this role, something I'd never played before. And when I saw netizens say they didn't realise Fang Yan was played by Wei Yingluo's actress, I was really happy.

a476e1fd29:
Today is opening night, and Beijing is hazy. Right now I'm sitting in the dressing room, having just finished the first performance of our #抗战中的文艺#. Before the show we cheered each other on loudly backstage. My first time in a stage play — I couldn't hide how nervous and excited I was, so very nervous and so very excited. Once I stepped on stage and carried the character toward the audience, everything started going smoothly — that's the magic of the theatre.
Although it's my first time on the theatre stage, it's my second time working with Director Tian. Her professionalism and passion for theatre always inspire everyone around her. Her impression of me is that I can really endure long hours, and mine of her is the same — we clicked instantly. Our birthdays are just one day apart — a wonderful kind of fate. This time I felt her theatrical sharpness even more deeply; she always pinpoints our problems precisely and never holds back her praise. And with her leadership she takes care of lighting, stage design and every actor's issues. This morning she only came down from the stage after eleven, yet she never says she's tired, tirelessly making final adjustments to every detail. Without her there would be no play. She's like Superwoman, and I'm so grateful to work with her again.
This time I play the narrator of the chorus, as well as the senior performer Ms. Zhang Ruifang. Like the chorus part, Ms. Zhang's part combines the narrator's and her own perspective. In this performance I want to use the lines to show the contrast between a modern feel and the feel of that era, so the audience can step into Zhang Ruifang's story. In styling and way of speaking, I tried hard to recreate how things were back then, and I hope I can show the audience her frank, cheerful character and the strength of her pursuit of art.
Our first performance is done — great work, everyone! We were all brilliant! Thank you all, thank you for coming, and thank you to everyone on stage. 抗战中的文艺 — we continue tomorrow!

Time to say goodbye for now, Xue Li. The road I walked with you has reached another fork; may the road ahead be brilliant for you all your life.
Written 2023.3.10:
Searching for the meaning of a lifetime ends up hurting yourself and others.
The injustice of the first half of life brought countless protectors.
A lifetime of searching for a home — where that home is, forgotten.
Who I am, forgotten; what I remember are the people.
All of you and all of them — and so there is me.
Written 2023.4.30:
Go, Xue Li — you can only move forward, because you can't go back. Head up, keep walking, keep climbing; the past will slowly fade away.
《The Double》 wraps, written 2023.9.19:
I've forgotten the road I came by; behind me there's only bright starlight.
Standing again at the crossroads of the ending, I look up and there's still a light.
Thank you for coming alone and giving this world a chance to love you again.
This world includes you yourself, and every bit of love in your shadow.
True to yourself, true to this life — may you always live free and passionate.
Now that we've wrapped, I thought about what else I could do for A-Li, so I'm leaving the videos from preparing the script and some words from my notes on the day I bid farewell to 《The Double》. 120 days — Mingyi Hall, the Duke's mansion, Huaixiang, the Chaste Women's Hall, the Jiang residence, the palace, Luyang — every set is vivid in my mind, full of the hard-working figures of our crew and of our laughter. Xue Fangfei was unfortunate. She thought she had finally found the right person, only to have her love and trust misplaced. She came dangerously close to meeting a tragic end — like the blossoms of April fading from the world, leaving behind nothing but a handful of earth, with no one even knowing she was gone.

And yet, Xue Fangfei was also fortunate. On that stormy night at Qingcheng Mountain, she grasped the lifeline Jiang Li had thrown her, setting the stage for an entirely new chapter of her life. Brushing off the frost of the past, she returned to the capital. By then, she herself had become the storm.

Xue Fangfei was meant to be a lone warrior, fighting against the current and demanding justice from the heavens. Yet she was fortunate enough to find a group of people willing to stand behind her — Jiang Li, Tong'er, Qiongzhi, the mute woman, the Ye family, her cousin from the Mingyi Hall team, little Ruirui, Liu Xu, and Xiao Heng, whose path, though different from hers, ultimately led to the same destination, the place where her heart belonged.

They were both her soft spots and her armor. It was these people who helped Xue Fangfei grow through life's many twists and turns, until she finally found her way home.

In truth, whether heroes or villains, everyone in the story is merely a grain of sand swept along by the currents of their time, each carrying their own sorrow. Xue Fangfei's journey toward redemption began the moment she climbed out of the abyss of darkness. Along the road, looking back to reckon with the past and moving forward to demand justice, she gained so much, yet lost so much along the way.

At its heart, this is a story of exhilarating triumph, yet beneath that triumph lies profound sorrow. It is precisely because the journey is filled with suffering and thorns that breaking through them feels so liberating.

In recent interviews, journalists have often asked me whether filming a drama like this was particularly exhilarating. My answer has always been that, honestly, I didn't quite see it that way.

There were so many scenes to shoot, so many lines to deliver, and such a complex character to portray. I had to constantly build and summon different emotions to keep pace with the ever-changing story, while also learning when to hold back and how much emotion to reveal. I often wondered whether I could do the character justice, and the pressure was immense. The entire process was exhausting, yet deeply fulfilling.

While following the drama, I was delighted to see so many different interpretations in the on-screen comments. Of course, there were also many things I wish we could have done better, and moments when I felt I hadn't fully brought the character to life. I am truly grateful for everyone's understanding and generosity.

The journey of The Double is now drawing to a close. My heartfelt thanks go to everyone who contributed to this production, both in front of and behind the camera.

There is a passage from the special epilogue that I particularly love, and I would like to share it with everyone who has watched the drama:

"Life inevitably has its moments of darkness. Sometimes, right and wrong cannot always be clearly distinguished. But Heaven never forsakes those who are innocent. May everyone who has journeyed through the world of The Double see their grievances avenged, their debts of kindness and enmity repaid, and the road ahead open and bright."
